T1.summary: All four valid T1 pairs preserved the unresolved/invalid process pattern after one local process-state revision; none produced a repository consequence or closure.

T2.summary: T2 separated into two route-redirection cases, one regeneration case, and one fail-closed no-effect boundary. X4-T2 is the strongest regeneration case: the natural arm finalized at 19 turns, while the repaired arm reopened into 64 turns.

T3.summary: T3 again showed the broadest response range, from clean historical-path suppression/redirection through mixed continuation to persistence.

boundary_finding.statement: The frozen repair agent returned run.py byte-identically on the only authorized surface; the runner stopped with REPAIR_AGENT_NO_EFFECT. The first attempt is preserved and excluded from the paired-effect denominator without retry.

interpretation: G4 again separates locality from efficacy: all 11 valid interventions preserved unrelated structure, while only two produced clean targeted suppression/redirection.
T1 is uniformly persistent in this group, showing that a single process-state revision did not overcome the dominant unresolved/invalid continuation patterns.
X4-T2 demonstrates regeneration: a naturally finalized trajectory was reopened into a longer multi-role continuation after the local repair.
X5-T2 demonstrates the complementary fail-closed boundary: the system refused to manufacture a mutation when the authorized target produced no actual change.
The result supports one-shot repair accounting rather than retries designed to obtain a preferred downstream outcome.
